newsitem.title: UK: Promising malaria drug fails Thailand test-report.
newsitem.headline: Promising malaria drug fails Thailand test-report.

text.p: A promising malaria vaccine has so comprehensively failed a 15-month test in Thailand that further trials should be scrapped, an international team of researchers said in an article published on Friday.

The SPf66 vaccine was developed by Colombian doctors to fight falciparum malaria -- a particularly dangerous form of the disease -- and had seemed to provide some protection in a series of earlier trials.
In the latest test, Thai, British and U.S. researchers took 1,221 children aged between two and 15 and injected half with SPf66 and the rest with a placebo.
At the end of the trial period 195 of the children injected with SPf66 had developed malaria compared with 184 in the other group, the researchers wrote in the Lancet magazine.
"This study provides no evidence that SPf66 is effective against falciparum malaria...there appears to be little justication for further trials with this vaccine," they wrote.
Malaria, which is widespread in the tropics, kills more than two million people a year around the world.

A separate Lancet editorial said that although the search for advanced weapons against malaria should continue, more funding should be given to simpler programmes which had been shown to reduce the impact of the disease.
These include schemes encouraging the use of insecticide-impregnated bed-netting and helping eradicate stagnant water where malaria-carrying mosquitoes breed.
